summary: Obligation to protect security and confidentiality of customers' nonpublic personal information; agencies issue safeguards standards (Interagency Guidelines, FTC Safeguards, SEC Reg S-P, state insurance laws).
applies_to: Financial institutions (banks, securities firms, insurers, nonbank lenders etc.).

short_name: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B (OCC); 12 CFR 208 App. D-2 & 225 App. F (FRB); 12 CFR 364 App. B (FDIC)
summary: Board-approved information security program: risk assessment, access controls, encryption, monitoring, service provider oversight, incident response and customer notice guidance, annual board report.
applies_to: National banks, federal savings associations, state member/nonmember banks, bank holding companies.
size_thresholds: No size exemption; program must be appropriate to size and complexity.

summary: Written information security program with qualified individual, risk assessment, access controls, encryption, MFA, pen testing/vuln scanning, service-provider oversight, IR plan, board reporting; FTC breach notification (314.4(j)).
applies_to: Non-bank financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction: mortgage lenders/brokers, payday lenders, finance companies, check cashers, wire transferors, collection agencies, tax preparers, non-federally-insured credit unions, investment advisers not SEC-registered, etc. (16 CFR 314.1(b)).
size_thresholds: 314.6: institutions maintaining customer information on fewer than 5,000 consumers are exempt from 314.4(b)(1) written risk assessment, (d)(2) continuous monitoring/annual pen test & semiannual vuln scans, (h) written IR plan, and (i) annual board report. FTC notice under 314.4(j) only if 500+ consumers affected.
status: Amended rule in force (86 FR 70308, Dec 9, 2021); notification amendment 314.4(j) effective May 13, 2024 (314.5).

summary: CISO, risk-based cybersecurity program and policies, annual risk assessment, pen testing, MFA, asset inventory, access privilege reviews, encryption, IR/BCDR plans, third-party policy, annual certification/acknowledgment, board oversight.
applies_to: Entities licensed/registered/chartered under NY Banking, Insurance or Financial Services Law (banks, insurers, agents/brokers, money transmitters, mortgage cos., virtual currency).
size_thresholds: Limited exemption (500.19(a)): < 20 employees and independent contractors (incl. affiliates); OR < $7,500,000 gross annual revenue in each of last 3 fiscal years from NY operations; OR < $15,000,000 year-end total assets (incl. affiliates) -> exempt from 500.4, 500.5, 500.6, 500.8, 500.10, portions of 500.14, 500.15 and 500.16. 'Class A company' = >= $20M NY revenue and (> 2,000 employees or > $1B gross revenue) in each of last 2 fiscal years -> extra duties (independent audit, EDR, PAM, password controls).
status: Second Amendment effective Nov 1, 2023. Phased: 500.17 notices Dec 1, 2023; most new reqs Apr 29, 2024; 500.4/500.15/500.16/500.19(a) Nov 1, 2024; 500.5(a)(2)/500.7/500.14(a)(2)/500.14(b) May 1, 2025; 500.12 (MFA) and 500.13(a) (asset inventory) Nov 1, 2025 - all now in force.

summary: Written incident response program; customer notification of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information; service-provider oversight incl. 72-hour provider notice; recordkeeping; expanded disposal.
applies_to: Broker-dealers, funding portals, registered investment companies, registered investment advisers, transfer agents.
size_thresholds: Tiered compliance: 'larger entities' (investment company groups with net assets >= $1B; RIAs with AUM >= $1.5B; broker-dealers and transfer agents that are not RFA 'small entities') had 18 months; smaller entities 24 months.
status: Effective Aug 2, 2024; compliance Dec 3, 2025 (larger) and June 3, 2026 (smaller) - both now in force.

short_name: SEC Regulation S-ID (Identity Theft Red Flags)
summary: Written identity theft prevention program for covered accounts.
applies_to: SEC-registered broker-dealers, investment companies (incl. BDCs/ESCs) and investment advisers that are FCRA financial institutions or creditors.

short_name: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668
citation: NAIC Model #668 (2017); enacted state-by-state (e.g., state insurance codes)
summary: Written information security program based on risk assessment, board oversight, third-party oversight, incident investigation, 72-hour notice to commissioner, annual certification (in adopting states).
applies_to: Insurance licensees in states that have adopted the model (adoption is optional and varies; text may differ).
size_thresholds: Model sec. 9: licensees with fewer than 10 employees (incl. independent contractors) exempt from Section 4 (information security program); HIPAA-compliant licensees deemed compliant with Section 4.
status: Model adopted by NAIC Q4 2017; only binding where enacted by a state legislature.

citation: 17 CFR 229.106 (Reg S-K Item 106); Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Release 33-11216, 88 FR 51896)
summary: Annual 10-K disclosure of cyber risk management, strategy and governance; Form 8-K Item 1.05 disclosure of material cybersecurity incidents.
applies_to: Exchange Act reporting companies (public issuers), including public companies in any sector.
size_thresholds: No exemption by size; smaller reporting companies received a later Item 1.05 compliance date (June 15, 2024 vs. Dec 18, 2023).
status: In force; effective Sept 5, 2023. No rescission found in Federal Register as of 2026-09-25.

short_name: NCUA security program and cyber incident notification
citation: 12 CFR Part 748 (748.0, 748.1(c), Appendices A and B)
summary: Federally insured credit unions must maintain a written security program meeting the Appendix A guidelines for safeguarding member information, a response program for unauthorized access (Appendix B), and must notify NCUA of a reportable cyber incident within 72 hours of reasonably believing one occurred.
status: In force (748.1(c) effective 2023-09-01, 88 FR 12811); proposals to remove Appendices A and B are not final

short_name: OCC heightened standards for large banks
summary: Covered national banks must have a written risk governance framework with independent risk management, internal audit, a risk appetite statement, and board oversight.
applies_to: OCC-supervised national banks and federal savings associations
size_thresholds: Average total consolidated assets of $50 billion or more (OCC proposal 90 FR 61084, 2025-12-30, would raise the threshold; not final)
